search tool seems to retrieve unrelated windows due to overlapping names. Hard.

Maybe easier to analyze logically: J74's single task had CPU request 1250? Actually job J74 has 4 CPU? Wait task shows: "860 T143 J74 4 1250 398 33 submit" indicates priority 4? but CPU 1250 memory 398 run time 33. So it's a production task (priority 4? Production tiers 9-11; so priority 4 is free tier). Actually 4 is free tier. So J74 task is free-tier. It ran on M06 from 867 to fail at 900 (33 sec runtime, so would have finished at 900, but it failed at 900). Wait deadlines: submitted at 860, started at 867, run time 33 -> would finish at 900, so it finished exactly at 900. But fail event 900 indicates machine M06 failed at 900? timeline: 860 submission, 867 start, 900 fail. That means machine M06 failed at time 900, causing task to fail. So J74's task was not important for later tasks; its failure may free resources earlier maybe affecting later starts. Could this affect T135? T135 start at 829 on M04. J74 uses M06, which might free at 900 for other tasks. However, J74's failure might affect which machine finishes first at 900? Not sure.

Given complexity, perhaps none of the provided statements would change? Let's examine each choice.

0: "task T135 would first start later than time 917 (its recorded first start), or not at all by time 1200". Recorded first start is 829. Removing J74 would maybe free machine earlier? It doesn't affect 829; so would start at 829 still. So statement false.

1: "task T225 would finish by time 1200". Recorded T225 start? We didn't find start. T225 is in list of submissions around 1183. Need to see if it finishes. It's priority 0, CPU 1250, memory 610, run time 1121? Wait earlier: T225 appears in submissions with machine? The record shows only submit lines; no start or finish. So T225 probably never started by end. Would remove J74 affect it? J74 frees M06 at 900; but tasks later may need that machine. T225 might be started later maybe after 1200? But would it finish by 1200? Likely not if not started; maybe if J74 removed, earlier machine availability could allow T225 to start earlier by 1200? But T225 might still be queued until later. Hard.

2: "task T170 would first start earlier than time 988 (its recorded first start)". T170 records: 977 T170 J86 submit, 988 T170 J86 start M01. So its start is 988. Removing J74 could allow earlier start? maybe but J74 was not competing for same machine? Might free M06 earlier such that T170 could start earlier on M06, but T170 uses CPU 937 memory 280? Wait the task line says: T170 J86 6 937 280 126 submit - runtime 126? Actually run time 126? Wait previous lines show: 977 T170 J86 6 937 280 126 submit -. Later 988 T170 J86 6 937 280 126 start M01. So start at 988. Removing J74 might allow earlier start? But J74 used M06; T170 on M01. However M01 may have had tasks that got freed earlier due to J74? J74 on M06, so no effect.

3: "task T180 would first start on machine M01". Recorded start? T180 appears at 1037 J93 1 1250 1553 254 submit, then later maybe start? Let's search later lines. After 1037, we saw later start at 1056? In the log we saw "1056 T180 J93 1 1250 1553 254 start M01" indeed start M01. So starts on M01; removing J74 probably doesn't change. So true.

Thus only choice 3 true. We must produce JSON.{"choices":{"0":false,"1":false,"2":false,"3":true}}

We need to determine which choices are responsible for eviction of T072 at time 359 on M01.

From events: at 359, T095 arrived (priority 9) evicts T072 from M01. Also T073, T085 also evicted? But question: Which of following are responsible for that? Condition responsible if without it T072 would not have been evicted at time 359.

Choices: 0 T070 submitted (running on M04 just before 359)
1 job J15 submitted
2 T069 submitted (running on M02 just before 359)
3 job J37 submitted

We must see if any of those submissions affect when T095 evicts? Actually eviction due to arrival of high priority task T095? Wait T095 is priority 9. But T071? Actually eviction occurs when a production task cannot be scheduled due to insufficient capacity, may evict. T095 is priority 9; it started M01 at 359. Meets scheduling round after failures? At 359, events: 359 T095 submit, then scheduling round processes waiting tasks. T072 was waiting? Actually T072 submitted at 230, started at 237 on M01. At 359, T072 is running on M01. The high priority T095 attempts to schedule; first fit: finds machine? M01 has T072 running; machine M05 down? etc. It may evict free-tier tasks to schedule itself. It evicts T072 because T072 is free-tier priority 0. So eviction depends on what machine had free-tier tasks. But other tasks running: T070 is running on M04; T069 running on M02. They are high priority (T069 priority? Let's check. T069 is job J30, priority 0? Wait in list earlier T069 J30 0 1250 283 252 in submit. So T069 priority 0 free-tier. T070 is job J31 priority 0. So these free-tier tasks occupy machines M04 and M02. The eviction rule: production task evicts free-tier tasks from one machine, starting from lowest priority then most recent. In each machine scans free-tier tasks running there. At evict, T095 will try machines in order. First machine with free-tier tasks that can be evicted to fit? It will evict tasks until fits. So T095 may evict T072 from M01 if M01 has free-tier tasks and evicting them allows room. But also could evict from M04 or M02 if those had free-tier tasks? They do. But rule: It will evict from one machine, evaluate each machine in id order: M01, M02, M03, etc. For each machine, considers free-tier tasks running there low priority first, most recently started first. It evicts them one by one until fits. It takes the first machine where this works. So given M01 has only T072 (priority 0). M02 has T069. M04 has T070. They all similar. The earliest machine where eviction works is M01 (ID order). So T072 will be evicted regardless of whether T069 or T070 present? If M02 had free-tier tasks, evicting from M02 would also make space, but algorithm picks first machine where eviction works. But M01 already works: evicting T072 gives free space for T095. So T072 eviction depends on presence of T095 and being able to evict? But maybe if M04 had no free-tier tasks, algorithm would try M01 then M02 etc. But with T070 present, M01 already works; still evicts T072. So T070 submission doesn't affect this specific eviction.

What about job J15 submission? At 65, many tasks of J15 submitted (priority 0). These tasks are running on various machines earlier. They might be running at 359? Let's check task logs: T050 J15 finished 368. Some J15 tasks finished earlier. At 359, J15 tasks include those submitted earlier? T050 submitted 65 with run 170, finished 368. T051 submitted 65, finish 445? Actually T051 finished 445. T064? Wait T064 by J25? Not relevant. So J15 tasks might be running but Finishing before 359. Some might still be running at 359: T049? Actually T049 J15 170? Let's look. But those tasks may fill machines? But even if J15 tasks exist, eviction would still happen for T072.

Job J37 submitted at 354: T092 (priority 4). That occurs at 354 before eviction. J37 tasks might be running at 359. But T095 arrives at 359; its scheduling round follows failures etc. At 354, T092 had start M07 etc. But presence of J37 tasks may not affect eviction because eviction only considers free-tier tasks.

Thus likely no choice is responsible. Therefore all false. Output {"choices": {"0":false,"1":false,"2":false,"3":false}}{"choices":{"0":false,"1":false,"2":false,"3":false}}
